questions.question: A company publishes a scaling policy describing its own safety actions and separate recommendations for the industry. What distinction should a reader track?
options: Which models appear in the examples and which do not
Which pages describe testing and which describe training
Which items are commitments and which are recommendations
Which items use short names and which use long names
questions.explanation: Separate Anthropic commitments from industry recommendations because only the former state what Anthropic itself will do; a recommendation to other labs is not automatically a binding promise by its publisher.

questions.question: What capability does the lesson associate with the AI R&D-4 threshold?
options: Generating a single correct code patch on a benchmark
Passing every current cybersecurity evaluation
Running a model without a human reading its output
Automating substantial AI research at competitive cost
questions.explanation: AI R&D-4 concerns automating a substantial portion of AI research at competitive cost relative to human-plus-AI work. A single benchmark patch or cybersecurity pass is narrower than that pipeline-level capability.

questions.question: What replaces the 2023 explicit pause commitment in the lesson's description of RSP v3.0?
options: A public vote on each model release
An unconditional promise to stop training at every threshold
Publish risks and mitigation case before scaling continues
A ban on publishing any new capability evaluation
questions.explanation: RSP v3.0 calls for publishing an affirmative risk-and-mitigation case before continued scaling, replacing the earlier explicit pause commitment. A promise to stop training at every threshold is stronger than the described process.

questions.question: Which document is forward-looking in the RSP v3.0 artifact pair?
options: Frontier Safety Roadmap
Risk Report
Safeguards Report
Capabilities Report
questions.explanation: The Frontier Safety Roadmap looks forward to planned safety work and expected capability; the Risk Report looks back at observed capability and residual risk. Confusing the pair reverses their temporal roles.

questions.question: A model meets a capability threshold under a scaling policy. What should the affirmative case cover according to the lesson?
options: A guarantee that no future deployment can fail
Only the model's training cost and runtime latency
The names of the teams that built the evaluation suite
Measurements, risk analysis, mitigations, and residual risk
questions.explanation: An affirmative case documents measurements, risks, mitigations, and residual uncertainty; it cannot guarantee zero future failures. The guarantee option promises more than the policy’s safety argument can establish.

questions.question: A reader sees numeric cutoffs in the lesson's toy evaluator and qualitative wording in the policy summary. What should they conclude?
options: Treat the code numbers as illustrative rather than policy thresholds
Use the code values to replace the source policy text
Treat qualitative wording as a typo without checking context
Assume the example's values are binding regulatory limits
questions.explanation: The toy code’s numerical cutoffs are illustrative, while the policy uses qualitative threshold language. Treating example values as binding regulatory limits confuses a teaching model with the source policy.
